day_local: Memorial of Saint Andrew Dung-Lac, Priest, and Companions, Martyrs
greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Grace and peace be with you as we gather in prayer.
penitential:
Lord Jesus, you lead us through every storm. Lord, have mercy.
Christ Jesus, you are the resurrection and the life. Christ, have mercy.
Lord Jesus, you hold our loved ones in your light. Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: The Lord comes to judge the earth.
homily:
Let us begin today somewhere very quiet, somewhere you can picture without any effort at all. Imagine a cold morning, the kind where your breath forms small clouds in the crisp air, and someone you love walks into the kitchen and sets a warm cup of tea down right beside your hand. They do not say anything grand. They do not give a speech. They simply show up, because they know you are tired, and because presence is the only language that matters when the world feels too heavy. That small, ordinary gesture—a warm cup, a hand on your shoulder, a quiet presence in the middle of a cold room—is where God so often meets us.

Today, in the readings the Church sets before us, we hear about harvests and sickles, about massive temples falling stone by stone, about angels crying out from heavenly altars. The Book of Revelation gives us this sweeping, almost overwhelming image of the Son of Man sitting on a white cloud with a gold crown and a sharp sickle in his hand, reaping the earth because the harvest is fully ripe. It is a striking image, vast and ancient. But let us hold onto one particular thread from it: the harvest. Not as a word of fear, but as a gathering. A gathering of what has grown, what has ripened, what belongs to the One who planted it in the first place. Every life that has ever been lived, every quiet laugh shared in a hallway, every brilliant thought and every gentle act of love—none of it is lost to the wind. It is gathered.

And then, in the Gospel, Jesus stands with His disciples as they admire the massive, costly stones of the temple in Jerusalem—stones so magnificent people thought they would last forever. And Jesus looks at them and says something that must have stopped their breath: 'All that you see here—the days will come when there will not be left a stone upon another stone that will not be thrown down.' He is telling the hard truth that everything we can touch in this world is fragile. The buildings we build, the plans we make, the days we wish we could hold onto a little longer—they slip through our fingers. He does not sugarcoat it. He does not pretend that life is easy or that sorrow does not visit the innocent.

We need to hear that truth, because pretending otherwise only leaves us more alone in the dark. It has been about five months since Benjamin Vo went home to God, and for Alan and Thao, for Ryan, and for everyone who loved him, the silence of that absence is a real and heavy thing. There are mornings when the house feels too wide, and evenings when the memories rush in like a tide you cannot push back. You carry the ache of a brilliant mind and a gentle soul—a boy who loved aviation so deeply he dreamed of an airline called 'Con Chim Airlines,' who coded games and applications with the dedication of a seasoned engineer, and who possessed an empathy so pure that at twelve years old, he wept at his father’s birthday simply out of the tender, premature fear of losing him. You remember the way he smiled through his braces, whether standing outside Saint Polycarp Church in a winter beanie or sitting on a snowy slope sharing instant noodles with his family.

Sometimes, in the quiet of the night, the weight of the "why" presses down. You replay the days, wondering if there was something missed, some stone unturned. Let us pause right here and let a healing truth sink deep into your bones. Illness is never a punishment, and it is never the fault of those who loved and cared for the one who suffered. God does not send sickness. Some sorrows simply come at random, entirely beyond human control, from nothing anyone did or failed to do, and no watchfulness could have prevented them. You missed nothing. You are not to blame. God does not accuse you, and you must not accuse yourselves. Lay that heavy stone down. You loved Benjamin with a love that was fierce, loyal, and absolute, and that love was his shelter every single day of his life.

Listen to how the Gospel turns. When the disciples ask Jesus when these terrifying things will happen, He does not give them a calendar; He gives them an anchor. 'See that you not be deceived... do not be terrified.' He speaks into their panic with a steady, unbreakable calm. He reminds them that even when nations rise and earthquakes shake the ground, God is not absent. The sickle in Revelation is not an instrument of cruelty; it is the hand of the Reaper who gathers what is precious into the safety of His eternal barn.

Benjamin’s life was short by our reckoning, but it was fully ripe in love. Think of the boy who, when his uncle William was struck by illness, unprompted and without hesitation, offered to give up his entire piggy bank to help. He did not need to smash it open; the gift was already complete in the offering of his heart. That was Benjamin—a boy whose first instinct was always to give, to share, to care. His love did not end on June 13, 2026. It continues to flow, just like the clean water of the well dedicated in his name in Cà Mau, bringing life to those who thirst, and just like the quiet, hidden acts of mercy done by those who keep his spirit alive in the world.

Ryan, you carry your brother’s laughter in your heart and his memory in your steps. Do not ever feel that you walk alone. The bond between brothers is forged in eternity, and Benjamin is cheering you on with that bright, familiar smile. Alan and Thao, your home bore the music of a brilliant, loving son, and though the silence is sharp now, his spirit remains woven into the very fabric of your family. He is at the Banquet of Heaven, resting in the peace that no earthly storm can ever disturb.

So what do we carry out the door today? Just this: take one small, deliberate breath of courage. When the grief ambushes you, whisper his name, smile at a memory of him talking about airplanes or sharing a warm bowl of noodles in the snow, and trust that he is safe in the arms of the Father. You are held, you are loved, and you are never forgotten.
petitions: For Benjamin, and for all who have gone before us marked with the sign of faith, that they may rest forever in the radiant light of Christ's presence, we pray to the Lord.
For Alan, Thao, Ryan, and all who feel the ache of missing Benjamin, that God may wrap them in His consolation, quiet their fears, and fill their hearts with enduring hope, we pray to the Lord.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot now receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, wipe away every tear from your eyes, and grant you His unshakeable peace. In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
standing_petitions: Benjaminilu kikkullu toqusimasut tamarmiusut Kristusip qaamanerani eqqissillutik naammassineqarnissaat pillugu, Naalagaq qinnuigaarput.
Kikkut tamassi nuanniilliorlutik aliasuttut, Guutip anersaakkut qorsuullugillu neriunermik tunniussivigissagai pillugit, Naalagaq qinnuigaarput.

readings.label: Atuarneq siulleroortoq
readings.text: Uanga, John, takuara pilersaarummillu pilersitaq nuiaq qaqortoq takuara, nuiallu qulaani inooqatigisaq inuup eriannik assigisoq ikilluni, niaquani qillaatissamik qulequtaqarluni, assaminilu sarsuussut oqummioqarluni. Malekat aappaq oqaluffimmit anivoq, nillialluni nuiallu qulaani inuusumut oqarluni: 'Sarsuussutit atoruk naajartortitsillutillu, piffissaq naajartortitsivik tikimmmat, nunap naasui naalluarmata.' Taava nuiallu qulaani inooasoq nunap qulaatigut sarsuussivoq, nunallu naasui naajartorneqarlutik. Taava malekat aappaq qilammi oqaluffimmit anivoq, taanna aamma sarsuussummik oqummioqarluni. Taava malekat aappaq altarimit anivoq, ikummatissamut nakkutigisaq, nilliallunilu sarsuussut oqummioqartumut oqarpoq: 'Sarsuussutit oqummiussat atoruk nunap viigisui katersorlugit, viigii naalluarmata.' Taava malekat nunap qulaatigut sarsuussivoq nunallu viigisui katersorlugit. Guutip kuffianut angisuumut igippai.

readings.label: Timmut Tusanngortoq
readings.text: Naalagaq nunap eqqartuussilerluni tikippoq. Kikkut tamassi ilisimassavarsi: Naalagaq tassaavoq Naalagaaffik. Silarsuaq pimoorullugu pilersippaa, nuussinnaanngitsumik; inuit eqqortumik naalakkersorpai. Naalagaq nunap eqqartuussilerluni tikippoq. Qilaat nuannaarlutik nunalu quviasulluni; tasersuaq tamakkulu imarisai nilliallutik; nunap silataat tamarmik quviasullutik! Taava qorsooqarfissuit tamarmik quviasuutigissavaat. Naalagaq nunap eqqartuussilerluni tikippoq. Naalagaq siornatigut, tikimmat; tikimmat nunap naalakkersornissaanut. Silarsuaq eqqortumik naalakkersussavaa inuillu neriunermik unneqqarissumik. Naalagaq nunap eqqartuussilerluni tikippoq.

readings.label: Guutip Oqaasia
readings.text: Ilaasa oqaluttuarimmassuk oqaluffik ujarassuarnik kusanartunik tunissutinillu pinnersagaasoq, Jesus oqarpoq: 'Utaqqisassi tamakku – ulloqartarpoq ujarak ujarammut ikkattoq unittoq anitinnagu taaneqarnavianngitsoq.' Taava aperivaat: 'Ajoqersuiyisoq, qaqugukkut tamakku pisussat? Aamma suuq taakkua pisussanut ersiutaassavaat?' Akivai: 'Mianersoritsi sallasitaaniarnarsi, amerlasuut aqqusaalermatik ateqarpunga, "Uanga tassaavunga", aamma "Piffissaq tikippoq". Maliganiarsinasi! Sakkortuunik ersinartunillu tusarnerni, ersinasi; taakkua siulliullutik pisussaammatata, kisianni annernanilu naggataassagunanngilaq.' Taava oqarfigai: 'Inuit inunnut saassussissapput, naalagaaffiillu naalagaaffinnut. Nunap sajuttarneri angisuut, kaattut, nappaatillu nunami sumiluunniit pisassapput; ersinartullu angisuut ersiutillu nukillit qilammit pisassapput.'

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: I miss you so much Ben! Ba má nhớ con rất nhiều mỗi ngày.
Nha Trang, ngày 31/10/2026, anh Minh suy nghĩ về Ben rất nhiều. Nhớ và thương em!!!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - mom and I have been missing you a lot.   Saw you a few times in my dreams last few weeks! Come and say hi daily okay?
Thinking of you buddy! Stop by to say hello whenever you can okay? Love you Ben

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - Been dreaming about you a lot. Hope you're having fun up in heaven. Please look after our family. Remember to come say hi daily. We miss you so much!

Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever
